item.title: Canada Fires Back in Trade War Against Trump With Up to 50% Tariffs
item.description: Canada said the higher levies, on items from aluminum foil to dishwashers to fish, would help protect workers, producers and manufacturers harmed by new Trump tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:credit: Jeff Swensen/Getty Images
item.media:description: The U.S. Steel Clairton Coke Plant in Clairton, Pa. Canada has announced it will impose retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent on hundreds of American products including steel.

item.title: Trump’s Canada Tariffs Rely on Untested Law
item.description: The president has invoked a long dormant section of law to hit one of America’s closest allies, a move that has troubled courts in the past.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump has invoked a little-known statute to impose his latest tariffs on Canada.

item.title: How U.S.-Canada Tariff Negotiations Turned Into an All-Out Trade War
item.description: Detailed accounts of the final hours of the negotiations show that, while the United States offered Canada what it said was the best deal of any country, what Canada had to give up in exchange was seen as unthinkable.
item.dc:creator: Matina Stevis-Gridneff and Ana Swanson
item.category: Office of the United States Trade Representative
item.media:credit: Andrej Ivanov/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada speaking about the trade dispute with the United States on Monday at the Davie Shipyard in Levis, Quebec.

item.title: At Least 1 in 4 NFL Players Gets CTE, Major New Study Finds
item.description: The actual prevalence, researchers said, may be much higher.
item.dc:creator: John Branch
item.media:credit: Zack Wittman for The New York Times
item.media:description: The biggest predictor of C.T.E. is the cumulative force of hits to a head over a lifetime.

item.title: Many N.F.L. Players Get Brain Disease. Why Hasn’t OSHA Intervened?
item.description: “We never see things that are this dire,” a former chief scientist of the agency said about rates of C.T.E. in former players.
item.dc:creator: John Branch
item.media:credit: Jason Andrew for The New York Times
item.media:description: The former N.F.L. player Jonathan Martin entering an M.R.I. machine for a brain examination that was part of a study to develop treatments for the symptoms and illnesses linked to C.T.E.

item.title: Your Child Plays Football. How Can You Minimize Risk of C.T.E.?
item.description: Researchers say it’s all about reducing the total number of blows to the head.
item.dc:creator: John Branch
item.media:credit: Brandon Thibodeaux for The New York Times
item.media:description: Many medical experts encourage children to play flag football rather than the full-contact version.

item.title: Fringe Views in Primary Campaigns Rattle Florida Jews

item.title: How the Supreme Court Is Issuing Orders as Trump ‘Emergencies’ Return
item.description: The justices are still struggling with whether and when to explain themselves to the public when the court issues temporary, but consequential orders.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston/The New York Times
item.media:description: In 19 months, the president has already asked the justices to intervene far more times than George W. Bush and Barack Obama did during their 16 years in office combined.

item.title: Supreme Court Allows Trump to Pursue Mail Voting Limits, for Now
item.description: The administration asked the court to clear the way for President Trump’s order that creates “state citizenship lists” and directs the Postal Service to decide who gets a mail-in ballot.

item.title: Trump Wants to Restrict Mail-In Voting. See Which States Rely on It The Most.

item.title: Trump Lawyers Warn That Kennedy Center Might Need Demolition if Not Fixed
item.description: In a court filing about honoring President Trump on the facade, the administration said that without a proper renovation the building might need to be “taken down.”
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:credit: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters
item.media:description: Lawyers for the Trump administration said in a court filing that if the Kennedy Center does not undergo planned renovations, it could be replaced by a large amphitheater overlooking the Potomac River.
